:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\textrm{rank}(A)$ is the number of pivot columns in $A$. 

Since $A$ has $7$ columns and $3$ of them are non-pivots, then the number of pivot columns in $A$ is 

$$
7-3=4.
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{rank}(A)=4$.

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Determining the Rank of a Matrix Given the Number of Pivot Columns

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Which of the following matrices have a rank of $4?$



$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}, \quad C = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that a matrix of rank $4$ must have at least $4$ columns and at least $4$ rows. 
So, we disregard the matrix $B$ since it has only $3$ rows. 

Also, the matrix must have $4$ pivot columns. As we can see, the matrix $A$ has only $3$ pivot columns, while the matrix $C$ has exactly $4$ pivot columns. So, $\textrm{rank}(A)=3$ and $\textrm{rank}(C)=4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only".

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Matrix With a Given Rank by Inspection

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
To find the rank of $A,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ -4 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 6 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 35\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has $3$ pivot columns (or, alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\textrm{rank}(A)=3.$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Rank of a Matrix Using Row Reduction

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
The dimension of the column space of a matrix $A$ is called the **rank of $A$**. It's usually denoted by $\textrm{rank}(A)$. So, 

$$
\textrm{rank}(A) = \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Col}(A)).
$$

For example, to find the rank of 


$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{bmatrix},
$$


we write $A$ in row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that there are $2$ pivot columns, namely, the $1$st and the $2$nd. This implies that the first and the second columns of $A$ form a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ and, therefore, the dimension of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is equal to $2.$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
To find the rank of $A,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ -4 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 6 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 35\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Rank of a Matrix Using Row Reduction

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Note that the number of pivot columns always coincides with the number of non-zero rows in the corresponding row echelon form matrix.
So, technically, 

$\textrm{rank}(A)$ is the number of *pivot columns* in the corresponding row echelon form matrix of $A$.

Or, equivalently,

$\textrm{rank}(A)$ is the number of *non-zero rows* in the corresponding row echelon form matrix of $A$.

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its pivot columns?


$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:



$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1} & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-1} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1}\end{bmatrix}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
The row echelon form matrix $C$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?



$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $C$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:



$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1} & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{5} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$



Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $2$nd column.

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by


$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by


$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}?
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+\left(-\frac{2}{7}\right){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & \end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.
